summary: Hydaburg Seaplane Base (HYG/PAHY) is a small water-based airfield serving the community of Hydaburg on the western coast of Prince of Wales Island in southeastern Alaska. As part of Alaska's extensive seaplane network, it provides essential access to this remote island community surrounded by protected wilderness and coastal waterways. The base primarily supports float-equipped aircraft serving local residents, mail delivery, and visitors exploring the Tongass National Forest region.
faqs:
Q: What type of aircraft can land at Hydaburg Seaplane Base?
A: The base exclusively serves float-equipped (seaplane) aircraft, as it operates on water rather than a traditional paved runway.

Q: When is the best time to fly into Hydaburg?
A: Summer months (May through September) offer the most reliable weather conditions, with calmer seas and longer daylight hours ideal for seaplane operations.

Q: Are there scheduled airline services to HYG?
A: No scheduled commercial service operates from this base; flights are typically on-demand charter operations serving local transportation needs.

Q: Is the seaplane base open year-round?
A: Operations are generally seasonal, with most activity occurring from spring through fall when waters are free of ice.
transport_tips: Access to Hydaburg Seaplane Base is typically via charter floatplane from larger hubs like Ketchikan or other Southeast Alaska communities. Ground transportation on Prince of Wales Island is limited, so arranging local pickup in advance is advisable. Visitors should coordinate arrival times carefully, as weather conditions in the region can cause delays or schedule changes.
local_tip: If visiting during summer salmon runs, ask your pilot about timing flights around fish counts at nearby streams—Hydaburg is known for excellent fishing opportunities that complement any trip to the area.
